rawOutput.rationale: Build the WWI cause map in one bounded sequence: first the prewar tensions, then the outbreak sequence, then the basic 1914 to 1918 timeline. This matches the learner's need for a big-picture start with visible steps, and keeps deferred future-session content out of today's work.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions divided Europe into rival blocs and made a local crisis more dangerous.
The Sarajevo assassination triggered the July Crisis, and mobilization and alliance commitments widened it into declarations of war.
The basic chronology runs from 1914 outbreak to 1918 armistice, with U.S. entry in 1917 as a major midpoint.
completionEvidence: Name the main alliance blocs and the tensions that made Europe unstable before the war.
Place Sarajevo, the July Crisis, the outbreak of war, U.S. entry, and the armistice in order.
Classify each major item as cause, event, or consequence.

methodBriefing.what: Study a clear model, explain it in plain language, repair any gap, then explain it again.
methodBriefing.why: Explaining the cause chain helps reveal missing links and builds a usable big-picture map.
how: Explain the idea from memory in your own words.
Compare your explanation to the model and fix the missing part.

Keep one visible action at a time.
Use the concrete example before the full sequence.

activities.label: Big picture model
activities.title: Europe before 1914
activities.body: Skim the model and note the main cause groups. Then pause and explain them back in one sentence each.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions divided Europe into rival blocs and made a local crisis more dangerous.

activities.label: Explain the outbreak
activities.title: From Sarajevo to war
activities.body: Answer from memory in a short chain. Then compare your chain to the model and fix anything missing.
activities.concept: The Sarajevo assassination triggered the July Crisis, and mobilization and alliance commitments widened it into war.
activities.correctAnswer: The assassination in Sarajevo triggered the July Crisis, and mobilization plus alliance commitments widened it into declarations of war.
activities.feedback: A complete answer shows the trigger, the crisis, and the widening steps. A common gap is naming the assassination but skipping how it spread into war.

activities.label: Repair the sequence
activities.title: Fix the war chain
activities.body: Use the cue to correct your sequence. Give one revised version with the missing step in place.
activities.misconceptionSummary: The assassination alone caused the war, so no further chain of mobilization or alliance commitments needs to be named.
activities.concept: The assassination was the trigger, but mobilization and alliance commitments widened the crisis into declarations of war
activities.correctAnswer: The assassination was the trigger, but mobilization and alliance commitments widened the crisis into declarations of war.
activities.feedback: The key correction is that the assassination started the crisis, but other steps turned it into a wider war. A full answer names at least one widening step.

activities.label: Timeline in your words
activities.title: WWI timeline check
activities.body: Say the main events in order from start to finish. Keep it to the five biggest markers.
activities.concept: The basic chronology runs from 1914 outbreak to 1918 armistice, with U.S. entry in 1917 as a major midpoint.
activities.feedback: A complete answer keeps the main markers in order and identifies 1917 as the midpoint. If you add extra details, keep the order intact.

activities.label: Recognition check
activities.title: Choose the timeline fit
activities.body: Pick the best match for the basic World War I chronology. Use the model if you need it.
activities.concept: The basic chronology runs from 1914 outbreak to 1918 armistice, with U.S. entry in 1917 as a major midpoint.
activities.feedback: The correct sequence starts with war in 1914, includes U.S. entry in 1917, and ends with the armistice in 1918. The other choices scramble the order.

activities.label: Return point
activities.title: Return to the cause map
activities.body: Write one thing to revisit later and one date to remember. Keep both short.

activities.label: Explain
activities.title: European alliance blocs
activities.body: How did prewar European alliances shape Europe before World War I?
activities.concept: Prewar European alliances divided Europe into rival blocs before World War I.
activities.correctAnswer: They split Europe into rival blocs, making a local crisis more likely to spread.
activities.feedback: The key point is bloc rivalry, not just the existence of treaties.
